item.title: [Sat, Jun 6] Bilingual Balance in Motion
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride Move, breathe, and energize in this dynamic bilingual class, led by Lauren Norton, designed to uplift your body and mind! item.title: [Sat, Jun 6] Lone Cone Librarys Annual Community Yard Sale & Bbq
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Lone Cone Library Norwood Our favorite spring tradition is back – the Lone Cone Library Community Yard Sale! Come browse treasures, support your neighbors, and enjoy a relaxed day on the lawn. Interested in being a vendor? Spaces are available for $10. If you’d like to reserve a spot, just fill out our quick sign‑up form at the front desk or below. Vendors are responsible for set up and clean-up of their items. Any items left behind will be taken care of in a respectful way (Donating, discarding, etc). 🍔 Community BBQ • 12–2pm Swing by for lunch while you shop. $10 per plate, includes a hamburger, a side, a drink and a cookie. Have items you no longer need? You can donate gently‑used items to the library ahead of the sale. We’ll add them to our tables, and all proceeds from donated items go directly toward supporting library programs.

item.title: [Fri, Jun 5] The Science of Connection: How our Relationships with Animals Shape Health and Wellbeing
item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Science & Innovation Center, TELLURIDE
Dr. Kevin Morris, from the University of Denver, Graduate School of Social Services, The Institute for Human Animal Connection (IHAC), will visit Telluride Science & Innovation Center on Friday, June 5th, for a presentation called "The Science of Connection: How our Relationships with Animals Shape Health and Wellbeing." Dr. Morris has done numerous studies and has worked with Veterans, prison inmates, underprivileged children and underserved communities to study and improve the bond and relationships between animals and humans. Free and open to the public.

item.title: [Fri, Jun 5] Town Talk: The Science of Connection
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Innovation Center What does science have to say about the bonds we form with other animals — and why do those bonds matter so deeply for our health? In this talk, Dr. Kevin Morris, American Humane endowed chair and executive director of the University of Denver’s Institute for Human-Animal Connection, explores the emerging research behind human-animal relationships and what it means for individual and community well-being. Drawing on a remarkable career that spans molecular biology, cancer research, and social work, Dr. Morris bridges disciplines to illuminate how our lives with other animals are not just emotionally meaningful, but biologically and socially profound. His work challenges us to think about health as something shared across species — and to consider what a more equitable, science-informed relationship with the animal world could look like for all of us. This event is free and open to the public but RSVP is required at https://form.jotform.com/ 261447761087060

item.description:

item.title: Lady Miners emerge as all-leaguers
item.description: The Lady Miners lacrosse team had their most successful season yet, finishing 6-2 in league and 10-5 overall before losing in the first round of state playoffs. Five players earned All-League honors, with Ruby Lake and Mikayla Ialeggio also receiving All-State recognition. The new coach emphasized how the team's chemistry and enthusiasm set this group apart from previous years.

item.title: We got us a posse
item.description: Montrose County's volunteer sheriff's posse is looking for more help, especially on the West End where fewer than 20 people are available to respond to search and rescue, fires, and emergencies across a huge territory. The all-volunteer group saves taxpayers money by handling everything from medical assists to crowd control, but they're stretched thin as recreational use grows in the region.

item.title: San Miguel County finalizes deed restriction reversions
item.description: San Miguel County commissioners have finalized a process allowing certain deed-restricted homeowners to revert to earlier versions of their property covenants after years of what some called coercive covenant changes during sales transactions. Of 206 properties reviewed, 31 owners chose to switch back to previous deed restrictions, with the county acknowledging "unintentional mistakes" in how they administered the housing program that began in 2010 and was amended multiple times through 2023.

item.title: All hail the queen
item.description: A local writer shares the story of a garter snake queen who claimed territory beneath a concrete slab, emerging each morning to sun herself on the lawn and raising babies over several summers. The homeowner carefully worked around her domain during mowing and trimming, but this year she hasn't appeared. These quiet wildlife dramas play out all around us if we pay attention.

item.title: Homicide convictions reversed for Colorado paramedics who injected ketamine into Elijah McClain
item.description: A Colorado appeals court overturned homicide convictions for two Aurora paramedics who injected ketamine into Elijah McClain in 2019, ordering new trials while upholding one assault conviction. The case, which resulted in rare criminal charges against first responders, has sent ripples through emergency medical services nationwide as paramedics now face potential legal consequences for split-second decisions during police custody situations.

item.title: Open letter to council
item.description: A retired developer with experience on major projects is urging town council to get professional cost estimates before approving the parking and affordable housing projects currently being designed by Design Workshop. The letter writer warns that neither Design Workshop nor town staff have the capability to accurately forecast construction costs, and argues council shouldn't approve projects without knowing what residents will be paying for in debt service.

item.title: Medically overweight or obese isn't healthy for pets
item.description: More than half of North American pets are overweight or obese, creating health risks like arthritis, diabetes and shortened lifespans. The local animal shelter offers a simple at-home test using your hands to check your pet's body condition by feeling their ribs. Bailey, a one-eyed shelter cat, is currently on a weight management plan and available for adoption.

Weather permitting, 15 balloons will also launch early Saturday and Sunday mornings from Town Park, flying low over downtown before landing near the Valley Floor.

item.title: Telluride Elks Lodge celebrates 125 years
item.description: The Telluride Elks Lodge is marking 125 years with 260 members across the region, operating out of the historic Swede-Finn Hall on Pacific Avenue. They've doubled their scholarship awards to $9,000 this year for six students pursuing any post-high school education, and continue hosting longtime community events like Turkey Bingo and Huck Finn Day.

item.title: Ted Turner has come and gone
item.description: A longtime filmmaker recalls making TNT's first original movie in 1988 and the nerve-wracking private screening for Ted Turner, who unexpectedly broke down in tears afterward because the father-son story reminded him of his own father's suicide. Turner called it possibly the best movie he'd ever seen and became a champion of the film, showing how even media titans carry deep personal wounds that shape their reactions in unexpected ways.

item.title: CHALKBOARD
item.description: This week's community birthdays include Lucas Priestley, Jodie Davis, Audrey Barrett Scholl, and several others from June 4-9. The Norwood Farmers Market continues every Thursday 2-6 p.m. through mid-October, while regular community meetings and services like the food pantry distribution on Sundays keep their usual schedules.

item.title: First Chair Destinations launches in Telluride
item.description: A new vacation rental company called First Chair Destinations has launched in Telluride, taking over properties previously managed by Casago and promising a more locally-focused approach than bigger platforms. The company is run by former Wyndham and Vacasa executives and manages about 3,500 homes across mountain and resort destinations in nine states.

item.title: Fresh Foundation, Food Hub: more than a farmers' market booth
item.description: Fresh Foundation runs eight food programs beyond their farmers' market booths, moving $1.4 million worth of local food through the community via wholesale connections, free pantries, senior meals, and markets in Mountain Village and Norwood that take SNAP benefits. They're addressing food insecurity that's easy to miss in our area — 2,400 people used regional food pantries last year, many just a short drive from the wealth of Telluride.

item.title: What if anxiety, perfectionism and people-pleasing are assets, not liabilities?
item.description: Attorney-turned-coach Jenny Robbins will speak at Wilkinson Public Library on Monday, June 8 at 5:30 p.m. about reframing anxiety and perfectionism as strengths rather than weaknesses. She'll share her personal story of leaving a 26-year legal career after a cancer diagnosis led her to build a coaching business, and attendees get a signed copy of her book "The Box."

item.title: Telluride Housing Authority launches tenant advisory committee
item.description: The Housing Authority is creating a tenant advisory committee with seven residents representing different town-managed properties like Shandoka, Sunnyside, and Virginia Placer. Committee members will get quarterly rent credits and meet at least four times a year to give feedback on housing policies and operations, with applications due June 17.

item.title: Curating good
item.description: Curate Telluride, a vacation rental management company, donated over $10,000 to local nonprofits this year through a program where they contribute 1% of commission revenue and homeowners match with either 1% of rental income or seven free nights for community use. The donations went to organizations ranging from the Mustang Sanctuary and Humane Society to youth hockey and the fire department. They're aiming to raise $50,000 next year.
